text: {"score":3,"justification":"Core numbers match the card (16.0% vs 3.9%, 11.65, z 2.15, 19%, 30 records, 2 of 24 no-lab, 0% vs 9%). The cited low-complexity claims fit the sentences. But there are several grounding and consistency problems that an investigator would have to untangle, and the 'at every complexity level' claim in the headline is overstated.","problems":["The headline claims 99215 is above expectation 'at every complexity level'; the card gives only provider share by band against the all-provider share, not the risk-adjusted expectation, so the wording is imprecise.","The '17%' (problems share) in the note checks is not on the card and is unmatched by the script; nothing here lets the investigator verify it. The late 7%, unsigned 0%, data 3% and 'no audit trail' statements are also not on the card.","The summary says both 99214 mismatches were documented at low MDM and claims 'a few repeated-time' signals, which is not in the packet.","Next steps are muddled: the first step says to request 99215 charts but names C0003446 and C0005118, which are 99214 claims; the narrative also recommends a larger 99214 sample, which the steps omit.","Sentence 'the provider's 99214 volume is also heavy' is unsupported as a concern; 1627 99214 claims is context, but no peer comparison is given.","Sample low-complexity claims are only called 'rash' for R21; R21 is rash, which is fine, but the example claim C0003482 (heart failure) is a poor illustration of a simple diagnosis."]}
